newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Thai-Philippine group puts land deal on hold.
newsitem.headline: Thai-Philippine group puts land deal on hold.

text.p: A Philippine-Thai consortium will refuse to sign a 1.58 billion peso real estate agreement with a Philippine government agency because of doubts over the exact area of land involved, the group's president said on Wednesday.

ML&H Corp president Sulficio Tagud told Reuters that the group successfully bid 1.58 billion pesos for a lease allowing it to develop and operate 247 hectares of land occupied by a former U.S. military camp in the northern Philippine hill resort of Baguio.
But a due diligence study revealed only 121.77 hectares was available.
"There is a huge discrepancy and we cannot proceed with the signing of the lease agreement until this concern is resolved satisfactorily," Tagud said.
ML&H was scheduled to sign the 25-year lease on September 8 with the Bases Conversion Development Authority, a government agency overseeing the privatisation of former military properties.
Officials of BCDA were not immediately available for comment.
The ML&H group is made up of Land and Houses Plc of Thailand, AB Capital and Asia-Pacific and Planning Evaluation Co.
